stem: During a procedure under general anesthesia, the client's temperature is trending downward despite passive blankets. Which nursing action best aligns with current perioperative temperature-management guidance?

options.A: Continue passive blankets alone because active warming is not recommended during general anesthesia
options.B: Initiate the facility's appropriate active-warming strategy and continue temperature monitoring, minimizing unnecessary interruptions to warming
options.C: Stop temperature monitoring once warming begins because a warming device prevents further hypothermia
options.D: Delay warming until the postoperative phase because intraoperative warming has little effect on perioperative hypothermia

rationale: AORN's updated Patient Temperature Management guideline emphasizes active warming because it is more effective than passive insulation alone at raising temperature and preventing hypothermia during general anesthesia. The guideline also emphasizes maintaining warming through the intraoperative and postoperative phases and minimizing unnecessary interruptions. Temperature assessment continues because warming does not eliminate monitoring needs.
educational_objective: When perioperative temperature is falling under general anesthesia, use appropriate active warming and continued temperature monitoring rather than passive insulation alone or delayed treatment.
source_document_title: Maintaining Normothermia: Implementing AORN's Updated Patient Temperature Management Guideline
